ai.summary: The agent runtime now supports an optional `completionCheck` that inserts a final verification prompt after tool work, provided the agent used work tools and the step budget remains. The SDK adds a `BACKGROUND` process type to `run_terminal_command` that spawns detached processes, writes logs to temporary files, and exposes `releaseBackgroundTerminalCommands` to transfer ownership. changes.what: Added `completionCheck` support to agent definitions and the `loopAgentSteps` runtime to trigger a final verification pass.
Implemented `BACKGROUND` process support for `run_terminal_command` with persistent log files and a process release mechanism.
Rewrote the `run_terminal_command` tool description to define authorization and execution scopes, and added a background process output schema variant.

eli5.text: The coding assistant now runs a final double-check of its work before finishing a task, asking itself if everything requested is truly done and fixing any last problems if the time budget allows. It can also start long-running commands that keep running in the background while it moves on to other steps, writing their results to files you can check later. This happens automatically inside the assistant’s workflow, so you simply get a more thoroughly verified answer without changing your settings or needing to wait for every single step to finish.

ai.title: Adoption watcher tracks package installs after ad clicks
ai.summary: A new adoption watcher in `cli/src/ads/ad-adoption.ts` monitors agent shell commands for package installs matching the vendor of a clicked ad, reporting a `postClick` engagement record when a match is found. The watcher parses commands in memory using `parseInstalledPackages` to extract package names from `npm`, `bun`, `pnpm`, and `yarn` install verbs, limiting the scan to the first 4096 characters and 64 packages per command to remain cheap. Wired into the ad click path via `armAdAdoptionWatch` in `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts`, the watcher is bounded to 8 concurrent watches with lazy expiration based on `AD_MS_CAP`. Six other changes expand the ad client context and engagement tracking with system, app, work, and network fields.

ai.title: Release 0.2.13 with ad adoption watcher and expanded client context
ai.summary: This release bumps the CLI version to 0.2.13 and ships the COD-757 wave 2 ad subsystem updates. A new post-click adoption watcher monitors agent shell commands to detect when a user installs a package from a clicked ad vendor, reporting a `postClick.packageInstalled` flag to the engagement endpoint. The ad client context and session snapshot are expanded to include terminal rows, system load, free memory, disk space, install method, and user typing rhythm, all reduced to coarse buckets to avoid fingerprinting.
ai.evidence: The diff in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` bumps the `version` field from "0.2.12" to "0.2.13". The release member source evidence for commit 3afeef582d36c7d102fa9a948438e9b9ec72b4a5 introduces a post-click adoption watcher (`cli/src/ads/ad-adoption.ts`) and expands the ad client context and engagement telemetry (COD-757 wave 2) to track idle time, keystrokes, tool calls, and system metrics.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the server-side implementation of the `/api/v1/ads/engagement` endpoint that consumes these new post-click and workload fields.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.2.13 adds a detailed activity monitor that records how you interact with the app to help measure ad performance. The release tracks specific details like which AI tool the assistant uses, how long it takes to show the first part of a reply, and whether you press keys while an ad is visible on screen. It also notes how much free space is left on your hard drive and how busy your computer's processor is, reducing all of this to simple, broad categories so no exact personal data is sent. If you click an ad for a popular developer tool, the app will quietly check if the assistant then installs that tool for you. The release also confirms that the /reasoning command is available for use in this version.

ai.title: Add COD-760 leg outcome fields to ad fetch telemetry
ai.summary: The `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` allowlist in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` now includes `first_party_outcome` and `house_outcome` to record the verdict of the paid and house ad legs on every completion event. The `no_fill_reason` field comment was expanded to describe a wider set of zero-ad causes introduced by COD-760, including refusal codes and Gravity outcomes. These fields are deliberately kept separate from `outcome` to avoid silently dropping requests from existing no-fill dashboard counts.
